scenarios.label: Vague criticism
scenarios.observedExample: I am hearing general dissatisfaction without a concrete example.

responses.grey: Which deliverable needs improvement?
responses.yellow: Thanks for flagging the concern. Could we look at one specific deliverable and the outcome you want?
responses.firm: I need a specific example and agreed standard before I can act on this feedback.

privateMantras: A vague criticism is not a complete assessment of my work.
scenarios.nextAction: Request a concrete example and expected standard.

scenarios.label: Guilt or loyalty pressure
scenarios.observedExample: A request is framed as a test of loyalty rather than a work priority.

responses.grey: What is the priority and deadline?
responses.yellow: I understand this matters to the team. Can we agree on the priority and expected completion time?
responses.firm: I can discuss the work required, but I cannot commit to unspecified additional availability.

privateMantras: I can care about the team without promising everything.
scenarios.nextAction: Separate the legitimate request from moral pressure.

scenarios.label: Dismissal warning
scenarios.observedExample: My manager raises possible job loss without specific measurable expectations.

responses.grey: Is there a specific performance concern I should address?
responses.yellow: I take that seriously. Could you identify the concrete expectations and what would demonstrate improvement?
responses.firm: Please clarify whether this is formal performance feedback and provide the specific concerns in writing.

privateMantras: A warning deserves clarity, not catastrophic certainty.
scenarios.nextAction: Record the exact statement; seek appropriate formal clarification.

scenarios.label: Public criticism
scenarios.observedExample: Critical feedback is delivered in front of others.

responses.grey: What specific issue should I correct?
responses.yellow: I want to address it properly. Could we identify the specific issue, and I can follow up with details afterward?
responses.firm: I would prefer to handle the detailed feedback in a focused discussion with specific examples.

privateMantras: I can remain composed without accepting humiliation as a definition of me.
scenarios.nextAction: Record factual points and request a separate clarification if needed.

scenarios.label: Gossip about teammates
scenarios.observedExample: A manager criticizes an absent colleague and asks me to agree.

responses.grey: What work needs attention?
responses.yellow: I appreciate you sharing the context. I'd rather focus on what we need to deliver together.
responses.firm: I'd prefer not to assess a colleague who isn't here. Let's focus on the project issue.

privateMantras: My colleagues are not characters in someone else's story.
scenarios.nextAction: Keep discussions task-focused; avoid repeating the gossip.

scenarios.label: The mysterious 'we'
scenarios.observedExample: Feedback is attributed to unnamed people.

responses.grey: Which particular issue is being raised?
responses.yellow: I'd like to understand that feedback. Could we review a concrete example I can address?
responses.firm: Please identify the specific concern and its source where appropriate; otherwise I can only respond to the stated work issue.

privateMantras: A vague collective opinion is not a verified fact.
scenarios.nextAction: Request one observable example and decision owner.

scenarios.label: Circular interrogation
scenarios.observedExample: Questions repeat while the original issue remains unclear.

responses.grey: Which question or event should I address first?
responses.yellow: I want to answer accurately. Could we settle on the specific issue we need to resolve?
responses.firm: I've answered the available factual question. I'll follow up in writing if more information is needed.

privateMantras: I do not need to defend a moving target indefinitely.
scenarios.nextAction: Capture the question and send factual follow-up.

scenarios.label: Changing criteria
scenarios.observedExample: A requirement changes after work starts or is completed.

responses.grey: What is the new requirement?
responses.yellow: Happy to adjust. My notes show the earlier scope; can we confirm the new acceptance criteria and impact?
responses.firm: The current documented scope differs from this request. Please confirm the change and revised priority.

privateMantras: An unrecorded change is not evidence that I failed.
scenarios.nextAction: Compare old and new requirements in Task Shield.

scenarios.label: Missing information
scenarios.observedExample: Required input remains unavailable after a request.

responses.grey: Which information can be provided?
responses.yellow: I'd be glad to proceed once I have the missing details. Could you share them or name the owner?
responses.firm: I cannot complete this dependency accurately without the required information. Please confirm the source and timing.

privateMantras: Missing information is a dependency, not a character flaw.
scenarios.nextAction: Log the missing dependency and request it in writing.

scenarios.label: Meetings without decisions
scenarios.observedExample: Repeated meetings conclude without action owners or decisions.

responses.grey: What decision are we making today?
responses.yellow: Happy to make this efficient. Could we agree on the decision, owner and next step before closing?
responses.firm: Before adding another meeting, I'd like to establish its decision objective and required participants.

privateMantras: A meeting is not the same thing as progress.
scenarios.nextAction: Send a decision / owner / deadline / unresolved summary.

scenarios.label: Unclear ownership
scenarios.observedExample: The team is asked to act but no one is assigned accountability.

responses.grey: Who owns the next action?
responses.yellow: To make sure this moves forward, could we name an owner and confirm the deadline?
responses.firm: We need a named owner and due date to treat this as an assigned task.

privateMantras: Vague ownership is a coordination problem I can clarify.
scenarios.nextAction: Record the owner or mark it as not specified.

scenarios.label: Micromanagement
scenarios.observedExample: Many approval checkpoints interrupt delegated work.

responses.grey: Which checkpoint matters most?
responses.yellow: I can keep you updated. Would one agreed checkpoint per milestone meet the need?
responses.firm: Could we define the review points so I can complete the work without repeated interruptions?

privateMantras: Oversight can be negotiated into a clearer process.
scenarios.nextAction: Agree on update cadence and decision rights.

scenarios.label: Conflicting urgent priorities
scenarios.observedExample: Multiple tasks are all described as the highest priority.

responses.grey: Which task should take precedence?
responses.yellow: I can make progress on both, but not simultaneously. Would you prefer A first or B first?
responses.firm: Given current capacity, A today means B moves to tomorrow. Please confirm the priority.

privateMantras: Capacity is finite even when someone calls everything urgent.
scenarios.nextAction: Get a written A/B prioritization decision.

scenarios.label: Credit for work
scenarios.observedExample: A contribution is attributed incorrectly or omitted.

responses.grey: I completed the initial draft of that part.
responses.yellow: Glad that work is moving ahead. For accuracy, I prepared the first draft and the team completed the review.
responses.firm: For the record, I authored the listed deliverable on the stated date; please update the attribution.

privateMantras: My contribution exists even when someone overlooks it.
scenarios.nextAction: Keep a factual contribution record without attacking anyone.

scenarios.label: Excessive workload
scenarios.observedExample: New work is assigned without resolving existing commitments.

responses.grey: Which existing task should move?
responses.yellow: Happy to help prioritize. With the new item, which existing commitment should shift?
responses.firm: I can add this only with a corresponding priority or deadline change. Please confirm which one.

privateMantras: I cannot create extra hours by apologizing.
scenarios.nextAction: Document capacity tradeoffs and requested priority.

scenarios.label: Excessive checking
scenarios.observedExample: Detailed monitoring requirements appear disproportionate to the work.

responses.grey: What reporting cadence is expected?
responses.yellow: I can provide regular visibility. What frequency and level of detail would be most useful?
responses.firm: Please confirm the reporting requirement and its operational purpose so I can apply it consistently.

privateMantras: Monitoring does not automatically establish poor performance.
scenarios.nextAction: Clarify reporting purpose and frequency.

scenarios.label: No answer to a dependency
scenarios.observedExample: An essential operational question remains unanswered.

responses.grey: Who can decide this?
responses.yellow: Following up on the open question. Could you confirm the decision or point me to the owner?
responses.firm: This task remains blocked until the listed decision is made. Please confirm by the agreed check-in.

privateMantras: Silence can be an unresolved dependency rather than a personal verdict.
scenarios.nextAction: Record the open question and next check-in.

scenarios.label: Concerning change after complaint
scenarios.observedExample: An adverse workplace change follows a disagreement or complaint.

responses.grey: Can we clarify the reason for this change?
responses.yellow: I'd like to understand the change and its expected impact on my responsibilities. Can we review it?
responses.firm: Please confirm the basis, effective date and implications of the change in writing.

privateMantras: A sequence of events needs facts before conclusions.
scenarios.nextAction: Record chronology; consider qualified workplace/legal advice if serious.

scenarios.label: Post-meeting rumination
scenarios.observedExample: I keep replaying an upsetting interaction.

responses.grey: I can write down the one relevant next action.
responses.yellow: That meeting was difficult. I'll capture what needs action and return to the rest of my day.
responses.firm: I need to stop working on an issue that has no further action today.

privateMantras: Remembering an event doesn't require reliving it.
scenarios.nextAction: Use three facts, one action and Closure.

scenarios.label: Ordinary disagreement
scenarios.observedExample: Two people propose different approaches to a real problem.

responses.grey: What outcome are we optimizing for?
responses.yellow: I see the benefit in your approach. Can we compare the tradeoffs against the goal?
responses.firm: We have two options with different costs. Let's choose based on the agreed criteria.

privateMantras: A disagreement is not automatically a threat.
scenarios.nextAction: Record decision criteria rather than personalizing the disagreement.

behaviors.title: Criticism without specifics
observedIndicators: A concern is expressed without a dated example or measurable expected result.
alternativeExplanations: Manager may have incomplete information or imprecise communication.
doNotInfer: Intent, diagnosis or legal wrongdoing is not established by this event alone.
behaviors.factualFollowUp: Request a concrete example and expected standard.

behaviors.title: Personal obligation in work request
observedIndicators: The request invokes loyalty, indebtedness or disappointment beyond the task itself.
alternativeExplanations: Manager may be expressing genuine urgency awkwardly.
doNotInfer: Intent, diagnosis or legal wrongdoing is not established by this event alone.
behaviors.factualFollowUp: Separate the legitimate request from moral pressure.

alternativeExplanations: It may be formal performance feedback; verify its status.
doNotInfer: Intent, diagnosis or legal wrongdoing is not established by this event alone.
behaviors.factualFollowUp: Record the exact statement; seek appropriate formal clarification.

behaviors.title: Criticism in front of coworkers

alternativeExplanations: A group debrief may sometimes be appropriate for shared problems.
doNotInfer: Intent, diagnosis or legal wrongdoing is not established by this event alone.
behaviors.factualFollowUp: Record factual points and request a separate clarification if needed.

behaviors.title: Missing task information

doNotInfer: Intent, diagnosis or legal wrongdoing is not established by this event alone.

doNotInfer: Intent, diagnosis or legal wrongdoing is not established by this event alone.
behaviors.factualFollowUp: Record the owner or mark it as not specified.

behaviors.title: Frequent approvals and checks
observedIndicators: Low-level approvals interfere with delegated work.

doNotInfer: Intent, diagnosis or legal wrongdoing is not established by this event alone.

behaviors.title: Conflicting urgent work
observedIndicators: Simultaneous assignments lack explicit priority tradeoffs.

doNotInfer: Intent, diagnosis or legal wrongdoing is not established by this event alone.

behaviors.title: Disputed contribution attribution

doNotInfer: Intent, diagnosis or legal wrongdoing is not established by this event alone.

behaviors.title: Unanswered operational request
observedIndicators: A decision required for work remains unanswered.
alternativeExplanations: The relevant decision maker may be unavailable.
doNotInfer: Intent, diagnosis or legal wrongdoing is not established by this event alone.
behaviors.factualFollowUp: Record the open question and next check-in.

behaviors.title: Adverse change after concern
observedIndicators: A negative change occurs after disagreement or complaint.
alternativeExplanations: Timing alone does not establish causality.
doNotInfer: Intent, diagnosis or legal wrongdoing is not established by this event alone.
behaviors.factualFollowUp: Record chronology; consider qualified workplace/legal advice if serious.

behaviors.title: Repeated mental replay
observedIndicators: An interaction keeps intruding after any useful next action is captured.
alternativeExplanations: The reaction may reflect temporary stress or unresolved uncertainty.
doNotInfer: Intent, diagnosis or legal wrongdoing is not established by this event alone.
behaviors.factualFollowUp: Use three facts, one action and Closure.

behaviors.title: Professional disagreement
observedIndicators: Two people disagree on methods, priorities or quality criteria.
alternativeExplanations: Different perspectives do not establish mistreatment.
doNotInfer: Intent, diagnosis or legal wrongdoing is not established by this event alone.
behaviors.factualFollowUp: Record decision criteria rather than personalizing the disagreement.

techniques.title: Grey Rock
techniques.mechanism: Brief emotionally neutral, task-oriented communication.
caution: May look cold or evasive when warmth or collaboration is required.

techniques.title: Yellow Rock
techniques.mechanism: Warm, brief and bounded communication without unnecessary personal disclosure.
caution: Can become appeasement if the user agrees to false premises.

techniques.title: BIFF
techniques.mechanism: Brief, informative, friendly and firm responses.
caution: Not a psychotherapy or guarantee against escalation.

techniques.title: Broken Record
techniques.mechanism: Repeat one reasonable request rather than endlessly justifying it.
caution: Do not ignore material new facts or keep repeating under threat.

techniques.title: Fogging
techniques.mechanism: Acknowledge a limited legitimate point without accepting an exaggerated claim.
caution: Do not concede facts you know are false.

techniques.title: DEAR MAN
techniques.mechanism: Describe facts, express impact and assert a concrete request using a DBT-derived structure.
caution: Real workplace power asymmetries may constrain assertiveness.

techniques.title: FAST
techniques.mechanism: Fairness, avoiding unnecessary apologies, values and truthfulness.
caution: Apologize when accountability is genuinely warranted.

techniques.title: STOP
techniques.mechanism: Pause, step back, observe and proceed deliberately.
caution: Not a substitute for immediate safety action.

techniques.title: Cognitive defusion
techniques.mechanism: Recognize a frightening thought as a thought rather than a proven outcome.
caution: Do not dismiss concrete danger or actual employment action.

techniques.title: Cognitive reappraisal
techniques.mechanism: Consider a less catastrophic interpretation still consistent with known facts.
caution: Do not use to explain away credible mistreatment.

techniques.title: Observer self-distancing
techniques.mechanism: Describe an event from an external observer perspective.
caution: Do not substitute detachment for necessary action.

techniques.title: Brief grounding
techniques.mechanism: Orient attention to current surroundings and body contact.
caution: Breathing exercises can be uncomfortable for some; make optional.

techniques.title: Controlled disengagement
techniques.mechanism: Request a brief pause and promise a defined factual follow-up.
caution: Abrupt silence can be perceived as refusing work.

techniques.title: Assertiveness and priority requests
techniques.mechanism: Ask clearly for objective tradeoffs and workable conditions.
caution: A manager may still retaliate; communication alone cannot prevent that.

techniques.title: Documentation and clarification
techniques.mechanism: Preserve accurate task facts and confirm decisions in writing.
caution: No guarantee of protection, legal outcome or confidentiality.

techniques.title: If-then planning
techniques.mechanism: Preselect a response to a recurring trigger before it happens.
caution: Plans should adapt when circumstances genuinely change.

techniques.title: Affect labeling
techniques.mechanism: Name a feeling in simple language to create a pause.
caution: Never infer feelings from user appearance or text.

techniques.title: Work detachment
techniques.mechanism: Capture necessary action, then intentionally stop replaying work.
caution: Do not ignore urgent duties or danger.

techniques.title: Supportive colleague relationships
techniques.mechanism: Seek factual clarification and social connection without counter-gossip.
caution: Do not pressure coworkers to take sides or reveal confidential details.

techniques.title: EAR acknowledgment
techniques.mechanism: Show empathy, attention and respect while returning to facts.
caution: Acknowledgment does not mean agreeing with accusations.

mantras.text: A vague criticism is not a complete assessment of my work.
I can care about the team without promising everything.
A warning deserves clarity, not catastrophic certainty.
I can remain composed without accepting humiliation as a definition of me.
My colleagues are not characters in someone else's story.
A vague collective opinion is not a verified fact.
I do not need to defend a moving target indefinitely.
An unrecorded change is not evidence that I failed.
Missing information is a dependency, not a character flaw.
A meeting is not the same thing as progress.
Vague ownership is a coordination problem I can clarify.
Oversight can be negotiated into a clearer process.
Capacity is finite even when someone calls everything urgent.
My contribution exists even when someone overlooks it.
I cannot create extra hours by apologizing.
Monitoring does not automatically establish poor performance.
Silence can be an unresolved dependency rather than a personal verdict.
A sequence of events needs facts before conclusions.
Remembering an event doesn't require reliving it.
A disagreement is not automatically a threat.
I am allowed to ask for a specific example.
An uncomfortable meeting is one event, not my whole career.
I do not need to invent certainty from an ambiguous warning.
I can be warm without sharing my private feelings.
My next sentence can be short and accurate.
Unclear expectations are questions, not proof of incompetence.
I can acknowledge a real mistake without accepting every accusation.
I can stop rehearsing a conversation once I have written the next action.
I can protect my relationships with colleagues directly.
No decision is still an unresolved decision.
I do not need to solve someone else's emotional state.
My financial needs are real, and so are my boundaries.
I can choose a professional response even while feeling angry.
I am experiencing fear; that is not a prediction.
I can give myself time to verify a claim before answering.
Other people's urgency does not erase the task constraints.
I can be courteous without agreeing to an inaccurate story.
Today's feedback does not replace my whole work history.
People can disagree with me without defining me.
If nothing further is required tonight, I may stop working on it.
One next action is enough for now.
I can ask who owns the decision.
I do not have to decode every hidden meaning.
A manager's tone and the actual request are different things.
I can let the meeting end, even if my thoughts are still loud.
My professional worth is not settled in one conversation.

tarot.title: The Royal We
tarot.fictionalSymbolism: The chorus speaks. Its membership remains unconfirmed.
tarot.groundedMantra: I can ask for facts without attacking anyone.
tarot.nextAction: Request one specific example and decision owner.

tarot.title: The Meeting Ouroboros
tarot.fictionalSymbolism: A meeting eats its minutes and summons a younger meeting.
tarot.groundedMantra: My time has value beyond the calendar.
tarot.nextAction: Ask for a decision, owner and deadline.

tarot.title: The Shifting Altar
tarot.fictionalSymbolism: The standard moves after the offering is delivered.
tarot.groundedMantra: A changing rule is something to clarify.
tarot.nextAction: Compare previous and new acceptance criteria.

tarot.title: The Golden Handcuffs
tarot.fictionalSymbolism: Coin and fear sit together on the same velvet cushion.
tarot.groundedMantra: Income is important and my judgment is still mine.
tarot.nextAction: Identify one practical step that protects your options.

tarot.title: The Inquisition
tarot.fictionalSymbolism: Every answer produces a new question and no stated allegation.
tarot.groundedMantra: I can return to the specific issue.
tarot.nextAction: Ask what single factual question needs resolution.

tarot.title: The Whispering Tower
tarot.fictionalSymbolism: Absent coworkers are quoted by a mysterious messenger.
tarot.groundedMantra: I can trust my direct experience of colleagues.
tarot.nextAction: Avoid gossip and focus on observable work.

tarot.title: The Tiny Crown
tarot.fictionalSymbolism: The title is large. The evidence is small.
tarot.groundedMantra: Authority does not turn vagueness into facts.

tarot.title: The Closed Portal
tarot.fictionalSymbolism: The meeting ends; the imaginary meeting need not continue.
tarot.groundedMantra: I may close this thought after writing the next action.

tarot.title: The Paper Moon
tarot.fictionalSymbolism: A warning casts a shadow larger than the available evidence.
tarot.groundedMantra: Fear is real; predictions need verification.
tarot.nextAction: Differentiate the exact statement from your feared outcome.

tarot.title: The Overgrown Process
tarot.fictionalSymbolism: A checklist has grown a kingdom of its own.
tarot.groundedMantra: A process should help a decision, not replace it.
tarot.nextAction: Ask which outcome the next step serves.

tarot.title: The Witness
tarot.fictionalSymbolism: A quiet notebook separates memory from interpretation.
tarot.groundedMantra: I can record what happened without diagnosing anyone.
tarot.nextAction: Write an observable fact and one follow-up.

tarot.title: The Open Door
tarot.fictionalSymbolism: There are more options than one frightened moment reveals.
tarot.groundedMantra: I can preserve my choices one step at a time.
tarot.nextAction: Identify one source of support or practical alternative.

corporateWeather: Mercury is in Scope Creep. Confirm the definition of done.
Saturn has entered the Approval Queue. Agree on a review checkpoint.
The Moon opposes the Royal We. Name the decision owner.
Jupiter has scheduled a meeting with itself. Ask what decision is needed.
Venus is in Yellow Rock. Be kind and brief.
Mars is behind on documentation. Write the agreed next step.
The stars request a single deadline. Two vague deadlines are not one plan.
The Office Nebula is expanding. Separate required work from optional work.
The Comet of Urgency passes again. Check what truly changed.
The Forecast of Feedback is cloudy. Ask for a specific example.
Pluto is in Deep Work. Close unnecessary tabs.
The Eclipse of Ownership is temporary. Assign a named action owner.
